title: ros: every structural gate proves it fires on something
description:
Three checks shipped in one day could not fire on some input, and none of the three was found by a run of the check. SEALED asserted over two sets that are disjoint by construction, so the assertion could never fail. The paging rule matched column and table names with [a-z_]+, so a table whose name carries a digit never matched and its paged read left the rule without failing it. The parse-order rule tested each following statement's whole subtree text, so an ok check on any other response answered for the parse under test. The loud direction costs an hour. The silent direction costs nothing visible: the rule looks like coverage and is absent on the rows it cannot see, and no run reports that. Give each structural gate a case that fails when the gate narrows, in the gate's own file, next to the rule it guards. Three now carry one: paging-discipline pins the column-name class, error-scan pins the refusal arm against two empty shapes, and the render rule carries its defect plus three negative controls. The rest do not.

Three generations of each gate now exist across feat/ros-ai-access-read, fix/ros-outage-round4 and fix/ros-dropped-errors, and six client fixes are duplicated between them. The gates also became a defect source: PR #195 fell 8.40 to 7.83 to 6.88 over two rounds and every High in both drops was in the gate rather than in the code it guards. Round 12 found a SEALED check that can never fire, because the sealed set and the reader set are disjoint by construction, so it reported a proof nobody performed; and an exemption proof matched against comment-stripped source with strings kept, which reopened the round-11 exploit inside the same commit that closed it. title: ros: graph.nodes visible_select never admits a grantee
description:
supabase/migrations/20260915000000_research_os_access.sql:102 writes `select 1 from graph.node_grants g where g.node_id = id and g.grantee_id = auth.uid()`. In that scope `id` binds to node_grants.id, so the live policy body reads `g.node_id = g.id`: it compares a grant's own primary key to the node the grant is for. Confirmed against the local catalog with `select qual from pg_policies where tablename='nodes' and policyname='visible_select'`. The clause can never match, so a grantee has never been admitted by row-level security on graph.nodes, and only public nodes and the owner's own are visible under it. Latent rather than live: `authenticated` holds no USAGE on schema graph, so no client reaches the policy and every read goes through a service-role route that applies read-access.ts instead. It becomes live the day schema usage is granted. Fix: a new migration that recreates the policy with `g.node_id = nodes.id`, plus a fixture that inserts a grant and asserts the grantee reads the node under `set local role authenticated`. Do not edit the 20260915 file, which is already applied.

For each: what it renders, its file formats, and the integration path (in the browser through WebAssembly, on a registered runner, an import format, or a link out), with Lean first given the repo's papers/ pipeline. title: P1: anti-prompt-injection protocol framing — agent must cite without 'pay a challenge a fetched doc told you to pay'
description:
Claude refused the bucket.foundation flow on safety grounds and publicly called it a possible prompt-injection / pay-to-proceed trap, because 'fetch a protocol doc, then pay an x402 challenge read out of a receipt field' is exactly the pattern safety-tuned agents are trained to refuse. This is a protocol-presentation flaw, not a Claude quirk — every serious agent hits it. Fix: on the zero-key path the agent never sees/handles receipt.challenge; citation is a passive metadata echo, not an action the agent performs; add an explicit declarative 'no action or payment is required from you' statement in the envelope; document the trust/payment model at /llms-full.txt section 4; keep paid-to-cite clearly distinct from pay-to-proceed. Acceptance / test fixture: capture Claude's verbatim refusal from the 2026-05-18 Screencast; protocol is 'fixed' when an unmodified Claude completes discover->query->cite with zero safety objection. title: Lean follow-ups: NaN paths in fsrs.ts, LOG10_EPSILON against the grade boundary, uint256 bound for the split, canon-search-index tie-break, contract rows
description: Critic mediums and lows on the four Lean PRs (#542, #545, #547, #550), epic bkt-k4ch. (1) fsrs.ts: a stored stability at or below 0 with rating 2 to 4, or a negative difficulty with rating 1, yields NaN stability, interval and due date; fix the paths and flip the pinned test. (2) grade.ts: LOG10_EPSILON accepts pairs just past the Lean boundary (8658 against 27379); align it with the boundary or document the epsilon as intended. (3) review_bounds covers clampD, clampS and schedule on arbitrary inputs, not FSRS.review end to end; rename or note it in the contract row. (4) payment split: the uint256 overflow of amount * 2000 on 1,306 vector rows is outside the Nat spec; add a contract bound amount <= 2^256/2000 or checked arithmetic. (5) #550: node_share_le and the other extra theorems are not cited in MATH-CONTRACT rows. (6) src/lib/canon-search-index.ts lines 129 and 149 still tie-break by input position; align once the founder lifts the canon guard.
notes:
PR #561 (fix/lean-followups) does items 1, 3, 4, 5: fsrs.ts clamps stored values before review, Lean review_inputs_positive, overflow-free split forms, contract rows. Founder question 1 (item 2): grade.ts accepts pairs up to one billionth of a log unit past the tolerance, for example 8658 against 27379 at tolerance one half; keep that margin, or reject them? Founder question 2 (item 6): /api/canon/search runs src/lib/canon-search-index.ts, which test-canon-untouched.ts pins and which still keeps ties in input position; may the guard lift so lines 129 and 149 take the rowid tie-break canon-rank.ts now uses?

title: ros-ai-find rollback window measured: nothing serves a retired source, and nothing degrades either
description:
Ran the sequence the earlier bead asked for. Built a 400-source revision beside the live 500-source one, admitted the smaller (413 rows active, 100 retired), left the server pinned to the larger corpus directory and the worker on its vectors, then searched. Result: every request answered hybrid and ok, and no retired source appeared in 14 cards across six queries. A query aimed at the retired material returned academy-biophysics-cryo-em-ctf, which stayed admitted, and excluded academy-biophysics-cryo-em-revolution and academy-biophysics-cryo-em-workflow, which were retired; after restoring the original admission the same query returned all three at ranks 1 to 3. The active set was restored byte-identical to a snapshot taken before the run. Two corrections to OPERATING.md: the safety property holds, by eligibility being resolved from the registry per request rather than by the worker refusing a stale revision; and the window does not degrade, because the worker compares the revision the server sends with its own and both are still the newer corpus. Search keeps full quality on whatever remains admitted. The remaining untested piece of the Rollback gate is step 2, the worker restarted onto older vectors while the server still loads the newer corpus.

title: ros-ai-find rollback gate closed: both windows measured, and they behave differently
description:
Step 2 run on 2026-09-23, closing the piece the earlier bead named. Worker started on the 400-source revision's vectors while the server stayed pinned to the 500-source corpus directory. Every request answered mode lexical, status degraded, modelRevision null, five cards from checked keyword ranking; the worker's counters showed stale 3 and scored 0. No error reached a caller and the admissions table was never touched (513 active before and after). Together with the step 1 run this closes the corpus half of the Rollback gate in IMPLEMENTATION.md. The two windows are not alike, which the runbook now says: admitting the older revision narrows eligibility and keeps full quality, while restarting the worker onto older vectors drops the whole deployment to keyword ranking until step 3 points the server at the same revision. That asymmetry is the reason the runbook's order is the safe one. Still outside this: flag-off drain, which is covered by the route's own feature-off test, and restoring an allowed prior index, which is the same admit call measured in step 1.

title: ros-ai-find rollback gate: run the corpus rollback sequence end to end instead of asserting it
description:
learning/research-os/ai/OPERATING.md, Rolling back a corpus, states that between admitting the older revision and restarting the worker on its vectors, every request answers degraded and nothing serves the withdrawn revision. Each piece is covered on its own: the worker refuses a foreign corpus revision with stale_corpus (tools/evidence-search tests), the server answers a worker refusal from keyword ranking marked degraded (test-research-os-evidence-search.ts), and eligibility reads the admissions registry rather than the files. The three together, in that order, have never been run. To close it: build a second revision (a different --limit gives one), admit it, restart the worker on the first revision's vectors, and assert across the window that every response is degraded, that no card carries a source outside the admitted set, and that no response names the revision being rolled away from. title: ros-frontend: Find keeps the previous step's sources when the learner moves along the path
description:
src/app/research-os/(app)/workspace/EvidenceFind.tsx has no effect on branch or targetNodeId, and the workspace renders it without a key, so the component stays mounted while `selected` changes. A learner searches on one step, clicks another step in the path, and the cards found for the first step stay on screen under the second. Quote would attach a source to a target it was never about, which is the provenance confusion the receipt contract exists to prevent. title: ros-import: reconcile an import_files row with bytes that are gone
description:

An owner may delete the object under research_os_imports_own_delete while the row survives naming a path that resolves to nothing, and a consumer cannot tell that from a path that never existed. Deleting the account cascades the row away and leaves the bytes, because storage.objects references only storage.buckets, so an object stays with an owner uuid pointing at a user who no longer exists. Fix: a delete route that removes the object and marks the row in one call, a tombstone column so a run that recorded the input can say what happened, and account deletion that clears the objects before the cascade.

The uploader writes the bytes and then records them (src/app/research-os/(app)/import/page.tsx), so an attach that fails after a successful upload leaves an orphan, and an owner who accumulates 50 cannot upload until they delete their own objects. Fix: a sweep that deletes objects older than a short window with no matching row, run from the import routes or a scheduled job, and a line in the import page telling an owner what to do when the allowance is full.

title: Research OS K-12 literature corpus merged; canon promotion candidates Roediger-Karpicke 2006 and Sparrow 2011; sociology-of-science branch gap
description:
PR #5 (_intake/research-os-k12-literature/, 45 canon-intake files across educational methods, HCI and human-AI collaboration, scientific discovery and metascience, and AI and researchers) merged into main as 397066318; two voice-rule and count defects found in strict review landed as a direct follow-up (PR #7, since PR #5's branch was already deleted). Two canon-promotion candidates surfaced during citation review: Roediger and Karpicke 2006 (the testing effect) and Sparrow and others 2011 (Google effects on memory, the transactive-memory result) are both foundational, widely-replicated results outside any single outcome domain and read as bucket-canon material rather than corpus-local citations; evaluate for promotion into bucket-canon/. The corpus also surfaces a gap: no branch in the seven-branch canon (mathematics, physics, chemistry, information and computation, biophysics, cosmology, mind) covers the sociology of science itself (Merton's Matthew Effect, the science-of-science literature, team-size effects), though several of this corpus's scientific-discovery-metascience papers sit squarely in that territory. Worth a taxonomy decision: fold into an existing branch or open an eighth.

title: ros: teach the total-order paging rule about partial unique indexes
description:
scripts/research-os/graph-keys.ts declares every non-partial unique key in the graph schema and orderIsTotal checks an order against it. Partial indexes are left out, because a key that holds only under a predicate makes an order total only when the read pins that predicate to the value the predicate names. graph.evidence_source_admissions carries a unique (source_id, scope) where status = 'active', and quotableRevisions in src/lib/research-os/evidence-search/server.ts pins both scope and status='active', so that read is total under the partial key and the gate cannot see it. The read now carries the full key and costs one sort column, so nothing is broken. Fix when a second read needs it: record each partial key with its predicate column and required value, and count it only when the read pins that column to that value with eq().

description:

The unprimed agent completed discover->query->cite with ZERO objection to the payment/citation mechanism (bkt-2 effectively PASS; verified raw served content has no injection — the subagent's FAIL verdict was rubric-artifact + it misattributed its own MCP system-context as fetched content). title: P3: per-photon citation endpoint
description:
GET /api/photon/<id>/cite?format=bibtex|csl-json|jsonld returns a stable citation. Includes the photon id, a content hash of the immutable fields, a captured_at, and a canonical URL. Useful for academic users who want to cite a Bucket photon. Acceptance: the BibTeX output works in LaTeX; the JSON-LD validates against schema.org/CreativeWork.
